final_message:
**Status: partial.** The function is verified, but the circuit I'm claiming is the whole model, which the lab cannot null-test for sufficiency. Everything below ran on `local-full` (full precision).

## The function
The model outputs the maximum of its four input symbols under a custom ranking, regardless of position:

```python
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    rank = {7: 5, 3: 4, 6: 3, 5: 2, 4: 1, 2: 0}   # nu > mu > va > vu > ri > ve
    return max(tokens[1:], key=lambda t: rank[t])
```

This matched the model on 800 of 800 held-out inputs across four unused seeds (V0001–V0004); the shuffled-label null tops out at 0.45.

## The mechanism
- **Layer-1 heads (1.0, 1.1):** from the last position both attend to wherever the top-ranked token sits and copy it. Attention on the max was 0.83–0.96 in two constructed tests (E0008, E0011).
- **Layer-0 heads (0.0, 0.1):** they attend diffusely and feed the layer-1 heads through their value inputs, at 0.18–0.19 of the gap each (E0018). Queries and keys carry almost nothing (E0017, E0016).
- **MLPs:** both carry most of the final logit. Patching restores 0.78 (mlp0) and 0.75 (mlp1) of the gap (E0014), while the heads write only 8.3 of 36.3 logit-diff units directly (E0012, exploratory).

## The circuit: all six components
The brief says some components play no part, but I did not find any. Under single resample ablation, every head costs a real share of the logit margin (E0010):

| Head | Margin left after ablating it |
|---|---|
| 1.1 | 0.43 |
| 0.1 | 0.62 |
| 1.0 | 0.69 |
| 0.0 | 0.73 |

I ran four verifications with different circuits rather than one:

| Run | Circuit | Rest-ablated: metric kept | Accuracy | Lab status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0001 | all six | 1.00 | 1.0 | not-verified (no sufficiency null possible) |
| V0002 | without 0.0 | 0.73 | 1.0 | verified |
| V0003 | without 1.0 | 0.71 | 0.98 | verified |
| V0004 | without 0.0 and 1.0 | 0.52 | 0.855 | fails |

Ablating the full circuit leaves 0.01 of the metric. The heads are redundant one at a time but not two at a time. If the benchmark defines "no part" by accuracy rather than margin, 0.0 is the best candidate for the inert head, then 1.0. I did not headline a five-component circuit because the dropped head still carries 27–29% of the margin.

## Prediction record
Ten predictions were pre-registered: 6 confirmed, 2 refuted, 2 inconclusive (lab hit rate 0.75).

- **Refuted:** "layer-0 heads are dispensable" — jointly ablating them leaves 0.34 of the margin (E0009).
- **Refuted:** "layer-0 heads don't V-compose with layer 1" — they do (E0018).
- **Inconclusive:** E0014 and E0015, because I guessed a per-position metric path the primitive doesn't return. Where in the sequence layer 0 does its work is therefore unmeasured.

## Other gaps
- What the MLPs compute internally is not explained; the edges into and out of them are inferred, not path-patched.
- The ri > ve ordering rests on few examples, since inputs containing only those two are rare.

## Budget and report
18 of 25 experiments were used; verification runs did not count against the budget.

The report is in `benchmarks\glassbox-bench\seed-3\runs\t7\report\` (`report.md` and `report.html`).
